description:
Sudan is facing one of the worst crises in education in the world. 
Since April 2023 conflict has forced more than 6,000 schools to close.
Many have been damaged and others are used to shelter families.
That means more than eight million children can't go to class.
They’ve missed around 500 days of school.
That's longer than during the COVID-19 pandemic.
But, unlike COVID, there is no online alternative, and children have been left with no way to continue their education.

Laura Frigenti is the CEO of the Global Partnership for Education. It's an initiative aimed at improving access to and the quality of education in developing nations.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The United States is implementing a major strategic shift on the Korean Peninsula, with a new Pentagon paper calling for South Korea to take the lead in deterring and, if necessary, fighting North Korea, whilst Washington steps back to provide limited critical support. 
The move marks a fundamental change in a security relationship that has lasted more than 70 years, during which some 28,500 US troops have remained stationed in South Korea and Washington has retained wartime operational control of South Korean forces. 
President Lee Jay Myung welcomes greater autonomy and wants control returned to Seoul, but the transition comes as North Korea continues advancing its missile capabilities and testing new weapons. South Korea has already received initial US approval to build nuclear-powered submarines and reprocess spent nuclear fuel, signalling a shift towards greater self-reliance in defence.

Al Jazeera‘s Jack Barton reports from near the DMZ, South Korea.

title: South Korea to lead its own defence as US steps back from Peninsula

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Haiti's transitional council has formally ended its term after a period marked by deepening insecurity, corruption allegations and political infighting. The nine-member body, installed in 2024 with backing from the United States and Caribbean leaders, was tasked with restoring order and organising long-delayed elections. Instead, armed gangs have expanded control over large parts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, and major highways, whilst killings, displacement and hunger have worsened. A UN security mission approved over two years ago remains largely undeployed, with fewer than 1,000 personnel, mostly Kenyan police, currently on the ground. The council's dissolution leaves Haiti facing renewed political uncertainty, with elections considered unlikely whilst gangs dominate the capital.

Al Jazeera's Alessandro Rampietti reports.

Heavy fighting in South Sudan's northern Jonglei state has displaced 280,000 people, with health facilities ransacked and humanitarian supplies looted, according to the United Nations. 
Thousands of civilians fleeing violence across the River Nile now shelter without adequate food, water, or medical care amidst outbreaks of cholera and malaria. 
The conflict has reignited ethnic targeting reminiscent of the civil war that killed 400,000 people before the 2018 peace deal, which observers say has all but collapsed. 
Survivors describe killings of relatives and desperate conditions in makeshift camps, whilst endemic corruption and the government's failure to deliver basic services continue to fuel grievances.

Al Jazeera's Malcolm Webb reports from Lake state, South Sudan.

Honduras's new president, Nasry Asfura, met with US President Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago in Florida, less than two weeks after being sworn into office. 
The visit follows earlier meetings with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as part of a diplomatic push to strengthen ties with Washington. 
Key topics include countering Chinese influence in the region, ending diplomatic relations with Beijing in favour of Taiwan, bolstering bilateral trade worth nearly $16bn in 2024, and addressing migration and drug trafficking. 
Trump previously threatened to cut aid to Honduras if Asfura did not win the election, and recently pardoned former Honduran president Juan Orlando Hernandez, a convicted drug smuggler, in a gesture seen as solidarity with Asfura's party.

Al Jazeera's Phil Lavelle reports from Palm Beach, Florida.

Palestinian authorities say bodies are often mutilated beyond recognition and returned without documentation on cause of death or detention details.
